terms.sub: Posture and Muscle Tone: Alpha-Gamma Coactivation, Stretch Reflex, and Decerebrate Rigidity
clues: It produces marked, sustained extensor hypertonia in antigravity limbs following high brainstem transection
In classic experiments, an intercollicular midbrain cut leaves pontine reticulospinal and lateral vestibulospinal excitation unopposed
Extensor tone predominates over flexor tone because higher inhibitory/modulatory inputs are disconnected

terms.sub: Cerebellum: Functional Divisions, Circuitry, and Motor Learning
clues: This cerebellar motor sign reflects an inability to accurately gauge the range, distance, or force of a movement
Patients often overshoot ('hypermetria') or undershoot ('hypometria') a target during finger-to-nose testing
It is commonly described clinically as past-pointing

terms.sub: Basal Ganglia: Direct, Indirect, and Nigrostriatal Pathways
clues: This dopaminergic projection connects the midbrain substantia nigra pars compacta to the caudate and putamen
Degeneration of this pathway is the hallmark neurochemical deficit in Parkinson's disease
It excites D1 direct-pathway neurons and inhibits D2 indirect-pathway neurons to facilitate movement

terms.sub: Locomotion and Spinal Circuits: Central Pattern Generators, Reciprocal Innervation, and Gait
clues: This neural circuit consists of coupled spinal interneurons that produce rhythmic, alternating motor patterns
It can generate coordinated stepping/locomotor bursts even without rhythmic sensory input or cortical drive
Higher brainstem centers and sensory feedback modulate its speed, timing, and load adaptation

terms.sub: Locomotion and Spinal Circuits: Central Pattern Generators, Reciprocal Innervation, and Gait
clues: This spinal wiring principle coordinates opposing muscle groups during reflexes and movement
When agonist motor neurons are excited, inhibitory interneurons simultaneously suppress antagonist motor neurons
Relaxing opposing muscles prevents co-contraction from braking the intended movement
